# Khedmah Google login — safe Floot editor fix (2026-11-06)

## Problem confirmed from source (candidate root cause)
The account Google login button previously waited for backend health GET, Firebase web-config GET, Firebase SDK script loading, and setPersistence before calling Firebase signInWithPopup. Async waits between user activation and popup may cause popup blockers to reject it. This is a browser-gesture risk, not proof of the whole historical login outage.

## Source-only repair applied to Floot editor
- pages/platform.account.tsx: preflight via react-query only AFTER a signed-out Khedmah session is confirmed; validate exact approved browser origin, healthy Preview backend, strictly allowlisted Firebase public config, SDK and NONE persistence.
- Disable Google button while preflight unresolved, erroring, or re-fetching; offer a user-initiated retry and generic safe diagnostics.
- Keep the existing button label constant for accessibility and tests.
- From the actual button click, synchronously call beginPreviewGoogle(ready.auth, ready.redirectDomainVerified) BEFORE handing the pending Promise to the useMutation used for session confirmation. No awaits between click and calling Firebase popup/redirect.
- Keep existing redirect protection: do not enable cross-origin redirect or alter Firebase authDomain; browser origin/identity restrictions remain strict.
- Keep no-session 401 distinct from errors; do not give admin permissions based on Floot auth.
- helpers/khedmahPreviewAcceptance.spec.tsx: regression proves synchronous Firebase popup initiation.
- helpers/khedmahPublicNavigation.spec.tsx: regression proves disabled Google until backend preflight passes, and refuses an exchange when unready.

## Verification

- TypeScript check clean before final checkpoint.

Public configuration API key was NOT logged.

# Google / Khedmah session-response contract — Floot editor only (2026-11-06)

## Verified problem and purpose
The prior `readPreviewSession` treated a successful status as a confirmed session if only `user.email` and `user.profile.displayName` were strings. It could return an incomplete typed object with no `id`, `status` or `profile.locale`. This was a client response-contract gap, NOT evidence of backend privilege escalation.

## Safe code change
- `helpers/khedmahPreviewLogin.tsx`: treat a 401 as signed-out (null), while all other non-2xx statuses remain `SESSION_UNAVAILABLE`.
- Parse 200 JSON with safe error normalization; reject arrays, missing user/profile and non-string required public fields: `id`, `email`, `status`, `profile.displayName`, `profile.locale`.
- Return only those required public fields rather than passing unexpected upstream fields through to the React Query cache.
- Deliberately preserve the backend's existing account status semantics: do not require status=active in the browser, alter session expiry, or infer admin access from this shape check.
- `helpers/khedmahPreviewAcceptance.spec.tsx`: negative cases for missing ID/status/locale, malformed profile, invalid JSON, 502 and positive case with stripped extra fields.

- 5 selected auth/role tests passed, zero failures; incremental TypeScript clean.
- Full explicit Floot Jasmine sweep: 139 of 139 spec files PASS, 0 FAIL (8 batches with 19 files each except the last batch of 6). Version tested `1793998971087`.

No tokens, emails or secret config values logged.

# Khedma — B2B public opportunity disclosure hardening — 2026-11-07

## Finding and data-flow assessment
The public business tender/detail and market opportunity list/detail endpoints already returned explicit public projections and applied safePublicText to some prose fields (location, descriptions). The public projection returned title and issuer/entity and sector without the same contact redaction. Since these fields may be populated by discovered or submitted opportunity data, an email, phone or detailed address embedded there could reach anonymous clients. This is a potential disclosure path demonstrated with synthetic fixture data, NOT evidence of an actual live data leak.

## Implemented in Floot EDITOR only
- endpoints/public/tender_GET.ts and tenders_GET.ts: apply existing safePublicText to projected title, issuing entity and sector.
- endpoints/public/market_opportunities_GET.ts and market_opportunity_GET.ts: apply the same existing sanitizer to projected title, issuer and sector.
- Do not alter canonical stored records, private/admin projections, public slug/identity, reference numbers, closing-date metadata, review snapshot or moderation authorization.
- Required title retains the string response contract, with an empty-string null fallback; unrelated public display fields and business review gates are unchanged.
- Added regression tests in helpers/businessTenderReviewedPublic.spec.tsx and helpers/businessMarketOpportunityPublic.spec.tsx with synthetic phone/email in public titles/issuer/sector; verify both list and detail responses hide contact data while preserving the public descriptive text and the original record.

## Validation
- Targeted related privacy/review tests 5/5 spec files passed, 0 failed.
- Full explicit Floot suite 139/139 spec files PASS, 0 FAIL, in 8 batches.
- Incremental TypeScript check CLEAN.
- Editor source version tested 1794001277542.
- This is NOT a substitute for a full data classification audit or malicious-content tests in all text fields and locales.
